requirementText:
# Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
MessagePack generated code is not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
There are no alternatives, it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases.

#### Additional context

N/A
author: Stelian Vultur
subject: implement issue #2297 : Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code

edits: +// Copyright (c) All contributors. All rights reserved.
+// Every occurrence of the attribute must be wrapped by the guard, so netstandard2.0 consumers still compile.
+// Formatters for objects (both integer and string keyed), the enum and union, plus the resolver.
+// Licensed under the MIT license. See LICENSE file in the project root for full license information.
+// The attribute is not available on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, so it is only emitted where it exists.
+/// Verifies that every type emitted by the source generator is decorated with <c>ExcludeFromCodeCoverage</c>
+IReadOnlyList<(string Path, string Text)> generated = await RunGeneratorAsync(TestSource);
+private static async Task<IReadOnlyList<(string Path, string Text)>> RunGeneratorAsync(string source)
+private static int CountOccurrences(string text, string value)
+All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, so generated code does not skew code coverage reports.
+The attribute is only emitted for targets where it is available (not `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework).

limits: Executed is not the same as correct: a covered line ran under a passing test, nothing more.
Coverage does not separate pre-existing tests from tests written in the same change.
Static reachability over-approximates: referring to a type is treated as possibly calling its constructors and framework entry points.
Calls made through reflection, generated code or analyzers loaded by the compiler are not edges in the graph.
Deleted code has no unit in a graph of the new code. It is listed as not analysed; what used it was not looked for.
Old and new code are compared only on the inputs a probe chose: no difference found on them is not the same behaviour.
The order of the list is a fixed rule over what was measured. It ranks where a mistake would matter and go unseen, not how probable a mistake is.
